answer: Agents can earn access to valuable tasks only after posting a refundable bond in a shared vault; peers challenge suspicious newcomers, and a proven duplicate identity loses its bond to the challenger or community. This makes mass registration costly: an attacker must lock real capital behind every Sybil and risks forfeiting it when identities are linked. A falcon-like auditor can flag clusters, while the tundra of ordinary low-value accounts remains cheap to ignore until they seek rewards.
